_comment: Ever or Never: Retirement Edition. Each statement is one short, specific retirement-life experience printed as 'Ever ...?' with an Ever box and a Never box to tick. Variety comes from structure, not paraphrase: every requested statement gets its own brief (a retirement topic and an angle, sampled by seed), so one reply cannot be twelve versions of 'taken a nap'. The model first names the one concrete moment that either happened or did not; a statement that is a vague habit or two experiences at once cannot be answered Ever or Never. The statement budget arrives on the request (frontend/src/utils/studio/ever-or-never/content.ts); limits below are the hard bounds. blockedTerms keep sensitive topics, ageist jokes and publishing risks off the page. participleWords are the irregular past participles a statement may open on after 'Ever' (regular -ed forms are accepted by pattern). qualifierWords are dropped before two statements are compared.

locale.nativeLine: - Write in clear, warm, natural English for adults and retirees.
locale.otherLine: - Write every statement in language locale '{locale}', natural for that language, keeping the 'Ever ...?' shape.

tones.gentle: Warm and gentle: a pleasant, relatable moment many retirees will recognise and smile at.
tones.playful: Light and funny: a harmless, cheeky little freedom of retired life that people laugh about and happily confess to.
